key_insight: An AI pathology model combining whole-slide H&E images and clinical data predicted both pathologic complete response and recurrence risk in HER2-positive early breast cancer.
clinical_relevance: If validated further, this approach could help identify patients most likely to benefit from chemotherapy de-escalation while flagging those who need more intensive treatment.
method: ATX NEO was tested for pCR prediction in PHERGain (n=306) and PHERGain-2 (n=383).
ATX RISK was evaluated for prognosis in PHERGain (n=309) using survival analyses.
Prespecified score cutoffs grouped patients into low, medium, and high response or risk categories.
evidence_signal: Continuous NEO scores were significantly associated with pCR in both trials, and RISK showed prognostic value in PHERGain with a C-index of 0.66 for event-free survival.
watch_item: These are trial-based retrospective analyses with prespecified cutoffs, so external validation and real-world implementation studies are still needed before routine use.
paper_title: Multimodal Artificial Intelligence Predicts Pathological Response and Prognosis in HER2-Positive Early Breast Cancer Treated with Chemotherapy De-escalation Strategies: Analyses from PHERGain and PHERGain-2 Trials
